## Motivation

@humansand

Prepare FlashInfer TRTLLM and CuTe DSL MoE decode profiles **plus exactly one prefill shape at startup**, following our [MegaMoE autotune design in #43789](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789). Decode-shaped warmup currently misses larger prefill inputs.

## Modifications

- **Profile set:** preserve native decode buckets through the graph/eager decode ceiling D, then add the exact prefill capacity P. Resolve P from the chunk buffer or scheduler limit and apply the actual DP gather width to both limits. No intermediate prefill sweep or rounding P up.
- **Lifecycle:** FlashInfer profiles the selected shapes during startup without enlarging the model dummy. The runner/layer retains the round-up mapping for serving; existing cache reuse and tactic synchronization remain in place.

**Example: D=32, P=5000**, with autotuning enabled. Startup prepares `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 5000]`. For the same kernel configuration, a **4000-token batch hits the 5000 profile and reuses its tuned tactic**. M is the MoE input token count after applicable DP gathering.

| MoE input tokens M | Serving selection |
| --- | --- |
| 1–32 | Native decode profile, including for a small prefill batch |
| 33–5000 | The single 5000-token profile; all inputs in this range reuse that tactic |
| Above 5000 | Native lookup or heuristic fallback |

**None of these serving paths enables autotuning.**

- **Controls:** honor `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`, deterministic inference, and `--flashinfer-autotune-skip-ops`. Preserve `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE` and `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`; disabling cache reuse still permits startup tuning. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND` controls only the extra full-model forward, so its default false value does not suppress this kernel-level prefill profile. A padded EXTEND dummy keeps the same profile set. Skipped ops retain heuristic fallback during startup and serving.
- **Scope:** regular TRTLLM/CuTe wrappers, standalone MXFP4/MXINT4, and Muse BF16. Draft and PD-decode workers retain their existing policy. MegaMoE, CUTLASS, and experimental LoRA policies are unchanged. Prefill-only precision/dispatch/finalization variants still need their applicable model hook or opt-in EXTEND pass.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Tested commit:** `287a1538bb1d6dd7fbac6841abead45e5a0616e6`, on C3 B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.
- **Existing suite:** `12 passed, 20 warnings, 8 subtests passed in 93.12s`. Scoped pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and eight CPU contract probes also passed. Only existing test fixtures/assertions were updated.
- **Native kernels:** both backends produced the exact seven-profile set. Serving and cache reload added no profiles; M=5001 used native fallback. The table reports the measured runtime inputs and output differences from the same-input heuristic.
- **Control checks:** disable/deterministic gates and skipped ops produced zero profiles; skipped serving performed no tactic-cache lookup. Padded startup M=5001 retained seven profiles and matched the heuristic. Existing tests cover cache reuse and the opt-in EXTEND gate.

| Backend | Profile count | Runtime cache hits at M=32/33/2501/5000 | Reload at M=5000 | Max absolute / relative L2 difference |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| TRTLLM NVFP4 | 7 | hit / hit / hit / hit | hit | 0 / 0 |
| CuTe DSL W4A4 | 7 | hit / hit / hit / hit | hit | 0 / 0 |

**Limits:** synthetic single-GPU kernels and existing unit tests. No model E2E, distributed MoE execution, full-precision model accuracy, distribution-aware autotuning, PDL, deferred-finalize, per-token-scale, or A2A result is claimed. Existing model E2E CI provides broader coverage.

[Harness, metadata, and complete result JSON](https://gist.github.com/zianglih/b7fce273f30a7f8f94dc790d57fe0735). Exact environment, reproduction commands, and complete raw output follow.

<details>
<summary>Environment, workload, and reproduction</summary>

- **Hardware:** C3; one visible NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) per process, driver `595.91.07`. The original run used GPU0 for units and GPU1 for native kernels, with separate cache directories; the commands below run them sequentially on one GPU.
- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261026-8252e3af`; amd64 digest `sha256:4e2b8a6f0b3ca9142639ceab2748c3e7ecee5923998928a457eb7e58b0307b2c`.
- **Software:** Python 3.12.15, PyTorch `2.14.1+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.
- **Workload:** TRTLLM NVFP4 and CuTe DSL W4A4; H=512, I=512, E=8, top-k=2, seed=42. Startup M=32, decode ceiling D=32, prefill capacity P=5000. Runtime inputs: M=32/33/2501/5000/5001; persisted-cache reload at M=5000; padded startup at M=5001.
- **Method:** native candidate lists unchanged; one warmup and three profiling repeats. PDL disabled in both arms. Outputs are compared against FlashInfer's heuristic on identical quantized inputs and weights. The 4000-token example above explains the mapping; it is not an additional GPU measurement.

  --output-dir ./results/single-prefill --backend both \

Closing this after tracing the existing behavior. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND=1` already provides opt-in prefill tuning for supported TRTLLM and CuTe DSL configurations. [MegaMoE (#43789)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789) retains per-capacity workspaces; the audited TRTLLM/CuTe paths do not retain a separate full GPU workspace per autotune profile, so that memory rationale does not carry over.

This PR adds kernel-level prefill tuning without the extra full-model EXTEND pass and replaces that sweep's intermediate prefill profiles with one prefill profile per kernel configuration. That trades shape-specific tactics for fewer profiling shapes than the EXTEND sweep, but we have not established a net performance or memory benefit to justify changing the existing policy.

## Motivation

@humansand

Prepare FlashInfer TRTLLM and CuTe DSL MoE decode profiles **plus exactly one prefill shape at startup**, following our [MegaMoE autotune design in #43789](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789). Decode-shaped warmup currently misses larger prefill inputs.

## Modifications

- **Profile set:** preserve native decode buckets through the graph/eager decode ceiling D, then add the exact prefill capacity P. Resolve P from the chunk buffer or scheduler limit and apply the actual DP gather width to both limits. No intermediate prefill sweep or rounding P up.
- **Lifecycle:** FlashInfer profiles the selected shapes during startup without enlarging the model dummy. The runner/layer retains the round-up mapping for serving; existing cache reuse and tactic synchronization remain in place.

**Example: D=32, P=5000**, with autotuning enabled. Startup prepares `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 5000]`. For the same kernel configuration, a **4000-token batch hits the 5000 profile and reuses its tuned tactic**. M is the MoE input token count after applicable DP gathering.

| MoE input tokens M | Serving selection |
| --- | --- |
| 1–32 | Native decode profile, including for a small prefill batch |
| 33–5000 | The single 5000-token profile; all inputs in this range reuse that tactic |
| Above 5000 | Native lookup or heuristic fallback |

**None of these serving paths enables autotuning.**

- **Controls:** honor `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`, deterministic inference, and `--flashinfer-autotune-skip-ops`. Preserve `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE` and `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`; disabling cache reuse still permits startup tuning. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND` controls only the extra full-model forward, so its default false value does not suppress this kernel-level prefill profile. A padded EXTEND dummy keeps the same profile set. Skipped ops retain heuristic fallback during startup and serving.
- **Scope:** regular TRTLLM/CuTe wrappers, standalone MXFP4/MXINT4, and Muse BF16. Draft and PD-decode workers retain their existing policy. MegaMoE, CUTLASS, and experimental LoRA policies are unchanged. Prefill-only precision/dispatch/finalization variants still need their applicable model hook or opt-in EXTEND pass.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Tested commit:** `287a1538bb1d6dd7fbac6841abead45e5a0616e6`, on C3 B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.
- **Existing suite:** `12 passed, 20 warnings, 8 subtests passed in 93.12s`. Scoped pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and eight CPU contract probes also passed. Only existing test fixtures/assertions were updated.
- **Native kernels:** both backends produced the exact seven-profile set. Serving and cache reload added no profiles; M=5001 used native fallback. The table reports the measured runtime inputs and output differences from the same-input heuristic.
- **Control checks:** disable/deterministic gates and skipped ops produced zero profiles; skipped serving performed no tactic-cache lookup. Padded startup M=5001 retained seven profiles and matched the heuristic. Existing tests cover cache reuse and the opt-in EXTEND gate.

| Backend | Profile count | Runtime cache hits at M=32/33/2501/5000 | Reload at M=5000 | Max absolute / relative L2 difference |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| TRTLLM NVFP4 | 7 | hit / hit / hit / hit | hit | 0 / 0 |
| CuTe DSL W4A4 | 7 | hit / hit / hit / hit | hit | 0 / 0 |

**Limits:** synthetic single-GPU kernels and existing unit tests. No model E2E, distributed MoE execution, full-precision model accuracy, distribution-aware autotuning, PDL, deferred-finalize, per-token-scale, or A2A result is claimed. Existing model E2E CI provides broader coverage.

[Harness, metadata, and complete result JSON](https://gist.github.com/zianglih/b7fce273f30a7f8f94dc790d57fe0735). Exact environment, reproduction commands, and complete raw output follow.

<details>
<summary>Environment, workload, and reproduction</summary>

- **Hardware:** C3; one visible NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) per process, driver `595.91.07`. The original run used GPU0 for units and GPU1 for native kernels, with separate cache directories; the commands below run them sequentially on one GPU.

- **Workload:** TRTLLM NVFP4 and CuTe DSL W4A4; H=512, I=512, E=8, top-k=2, seed=42. Startup M=32, decode ceiling D=32, prefill capacity P=5000. Runtime inputs: M=32/33/2501/5000/5001; persisted-cache reload at M=5000; padded startup at M=5001.
- **Method:** native candidate lists unchanged; one warmup and three profiling repeats. PDL disabled in both arms. @@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+"""Decode profiles plus one prefill profile for FlashInfer MoE startup tuning."""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from functools import cache, wraps
+
+_active_limits = ContextVar("flashinfer_moe_autotune_limits", default=None)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def flashinfer_moe_autotune_context(
+    *,
+    decode_num_tokens: int,
+    prefill_num_tokens: int,
+    skip_ops: set[str] | frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+):
+    token = _active_limits.set(
+        (decode_num_tokens, prefill_num_tokens, frozenset(skip_ops))
+    )
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _active_limits.reset(token)
+
+
+@cache
+def _tuning_buckets(decode_num_tokens: int, prefill_num_tokens: int):
+    from flashinfer.fused_moe.utils import get_hybrid_num_tokens_buckets
+
+    # Preserve native decode spacing; add only the exact prefill shape.
+    return tuple(
+        sorted(
+            set(get_hybrid_num_tokens_buckets(decode_num_tokens)) | {prefill_num_tokens}
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def flashinfer_moe_autotune(num_tokens: int, owner):
+    """Install profiles at startup and reuse their mapping during serving.
+
+    The owner is a persistent runner config or layer, never per-call quant_info.
+    Draft/PD-decode startup installs no override on its own owners.
+    """
+    limits = _active_limits.get()
+    if limits is not None:
+        decode_num_tokens, prefill_num_tokens, skip_ops = limits
+        owner._flashinfer_moe_tuning_policy = (
+            (_tuning_buckets(decode_num_tokens, prefill_num_tokens), skip_ops)
+            if decode_num_tokens and prefill_num_tokens
+            else None
+        )
+    policy = getattr(owner, "_flashinfer_moe_tuning_policy", None)
+    if policy is None:
+        return nullcontext()
+
+    from flashinfer.autotuner import autotune
+
+    buckets, skip_ops = policy
+    if num_tokens > buckets[-1] and limits is None:
+        # Do not clamp an oversized serving input to an undersized profile.
+        return autotune(False, skip_ops=skip_ops) if skip_ops else nullcontext()
+
+    # False inherits the enclosing startup autotune(True), but never enables
+    # profiling in serving. Both phases must use the same sparse ceil mapping:
+    # every token count above decode and through prefill selects the one prefill.
+    # An opt-in EXTEND dummy can be padded above prefill; still tune only this set.
+    # Keep skipped ops on their heuristic path before any mapped cache lookup.
+    return autotune(False, tuning_buckets=buckets, round_up=True, skip_ops=skip_ops)
+
+
+def flashinfer_moe_autotune_fused_func(func):
+    @wraps(func)
+    def wrapped(dispatch_output, quant_info, runner_config, *args, **kwargs):
+        with flashinfer_moe_autotune(
+            dispatch_output.hidden_states.shape[0], runner_config
+        ):
+            return func(dispatch_output, quant_info, runner_config, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    return wrapped

issue_comments.body:
Closing this after tracing the existing behavior. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND=1` already provides opt-in prefill tuning for supported TRTLLM and CuTe DSL configurations. [MegaMoE (#43789)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789) retains per-capacity workspaces; the audited TRTLLM/CuTe paths do not retain a separate full GPU workspace per autotune profile, so that memory rationale does not carry over.

This PR adds kernel-level prefill tuning without the extra full-model EXTEND pass and replaces that sweep's intermediate prefill profiles with one prefill profile per kernel configuration. That trades shape-specific tactics for fewer profiling shapes than the EXTEND sweep, but we have not established a net performance or memory benefit to justify changing the existing policy.
